collection.variants.ta1600-20-range.summ: The /20-3 configuration added a fixed and removable disk unit to the /20 range.
collection.variants.olivetti-m4-75-133-r: Olivetti’s service guide lists eight M4 configurations with Pentium processors from 75 to 133 MHz. The S suffix denotes the Slim Tin case instead of the standard Tin case.
collection.variants.olivetti-m4-pxx-rang: The M4-Pxx series comprises seven ISA/PCI configurations in Tin and Slim Tin cases. The service guide distinguishes Socket 5 and Socket 7 boards.
collection.variants.olivetti-pcs-51xx-ra: The PCS 5120, 5130 and 5140 shipped in Slim Tin cases with 75, 100 and 133 MHz Pentium processors, respectively.
collection.variants.olivetti-pcs-61xx-ra: The PCS 6120 through 6160 were sold in Tin cases with five factory Pentium configurations from 75 to 166 MHz.
collection.variants.olivetti-pcs-pxx-ran: Olivetti documented eight Pentium configurations from 75 to 133 MHz. E/En models came in Tin cases and n models in Slim Tin cases.
collection.variants.olivetti-pcs-d4-100-: Both versions have a 100 MHz DX4 and 128 KB of L2 cache. The En uses a Tin case and the n uses a Slim Tin case.
collection.variants.olivetti-echos-p-199: The range covered by MCmicrocomputer in 1995 paired a 75 MHz Pentium with a DSTN display or a 90 MHz Pentium with a 10.4- or 11.8-inch TFT display.
collection.variants.olivetti-echos-p-us-: The 1996 US range comprised four Pentium notebooks from 100 to 133 MHz. The processor and display varied, and all four shared a modular bay.
collection.variants.olivetti-m6-640-rang: The guide distinguishes the M6-640 with one 90 or 100 MHz Pentium and the M6-640 DP with two 90 MHz Pentiums.
collection.variants.olivetti-m6-650-690-: The guide lists seven Pentium configurations from 100 to 166 MHz in Tin cases. The DP variants shipped with two processors.
